nodes.summary: `k` is in its noncritical section; or `k` is choosing and either has still to read `number[i]` or its running maximum already bounds `number[i]`; or `k` holds a ticket and `(number[i], i) < (number[k], k)`. Whatever `k` does next, it does not overtake `i`.
nodes.title: Process `i` is ahead of process `k`

nodes.summary: In every reachable state of the bakery algorithm: if process $i$ is in its critical section and a process $k \ne i$ holds a ticket, then $(\text{number}[i], i) < (\text{number}[k], k)$ in Lamport's order.
nodes.title: Assertion 2 of the bakery proof

nodes.summary: `(n, i) < (m, k)` when `n < m`, or `n = m` and `i < k` (Lamport 1974, p. 454).
nodes.title: Lamport's order on (ticket, name) pairs

nodes.summary: The process has written `number[i]` and has not left its critical section or failed. Lamport's "in the bakery" starts one step later, when `choosing[i]` is reset.
nodes.title: Holding a ticket

nodes.summary: The process has set `choosing[i]` and not yet reset it (Lamport 1974, p. 454).
nodes.title: In the doorway

nodes.summary: Every process in its noncritical section, all entries zero (Lamport 1974: execution begins in the noncritical section; the arrays are initially zero).
nodes.title: Initial state of the bakery algorithm

nodes.summary: In every state reachable from the initial state of the bakery algorithm, every process satisfies the per-process invariant. It holds initially, a step of another process preserves it, and a step of the process itself preserves it given the invariants of all processes; CSLib's `mtrInv_of_trInv` extends this to multistep runs.
nodes.title: The bakery invariant holds in every reachable state

nodes.summary: If process $i$ satisfies the per-process invariant and a different process $p$ takes one atomic action, then $i$ still satisfies it. The values of $i$ do not change; the only work is to check that $p$, whatever it does, stays behind $i$ when it was behind $i$, and that a process $p$ that $i$ is about to read at L3 is still either behind $i$ or waiting.
nodes.title: A step of another process preserves the invariant of process `i`

nodes.summary: If every process satisfies the per-process invariant and process $i$ takes one atomic action, then $i$ satisfies the invariant afterwards. The two informative cases are the loop statements. At L2, reading `choosing[j] = 0` means that $j$ is not in the doorway, so it is in its noncritical section (hence behind $i$) or holds a ticket and is no longer choosing. At L3, passing $j$ while $j$ holds a ticket means that…
nodes.title: A step of process `i` preserves its own invariant

nodes.title: The per-process invariant of the bakery algorithm

nodes.summary: The atomic actions of process $p$ in the bakery algorithm, each given by its new program counter and its new values of `choosing[p]` and `number[p]`:
nodes.title: One atomic action of process `p`

nodes.summary: The bakery algorithm as a CSLib labelled transition system; the label is the process that takes the step.
nodes.title: The bakery algorithm as a CSLib labelled transition system

nodes.summary: In every state reachable from the initial state of the bakery algorithm, if processes $i$ and $k$ are both in their critical sections then $i = k$. This is condition 1 of the problem as Lamport states it ("At any time, at most one computer may be in its critical section"), which he derives from Assertion 2.
nodes.title: Mutual exclusion for the bakery algorithm

nodes.summary: `doorway U m`: choosing, with the entries `U` still to read and running maximum `m`; `write m`: about to write the ticket `1 + m`; `exit`: about to reset `choosing`; `l2 j` and `l3 j`: at statements L2 and L3 of the loop, for index `j`.
nodes.title: Program counter of a bakery process

nodes.summary: The state after process `p` sets its program counter, `choosing[p]` and `number[p]`.
nodes.title: Update by one process

nodes.summary: A state of the bakery algorithm for $N$ processes consists of a program counter for each process and the two shared arrays: `choosing`, a Boolean per process (Lamport's $0$ or $1$), and `number`, a natural-number ticket per process.
nodes.title: State of the bakery algorithm

nodes.summary: The process is in the loop L2–L3 or in its critical section.
nodes.title: Waiting or critical

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
